ashenvale_dryads_gone_quiet.accept_text:
The dryads answer when I sing. That is not a courtesy and it is not training - it is simply how it has always worked here, for as long as there has been a Grove to sing in.

They have not answered for a week.

I have been down there every evening. I have sung the calls they answer, and the old calls my teacher used before me, and last night I sang one I am not supposed to use outside of need. Nothing.

The corruption is in them now. It will not leave on its own and it will not leave because I ask it to; I have established both of those at some cost to my dignity.

I am sorry to ask you to release them. I am sorrier that I cannot do it myself without my voice being the last thing they hear.

Moonwhisper Grove lies east of Astranaar, near the border of the eastern woods. Go and see what has stopped them answering.

ashenvale_night_run_watch.accept_text:
Eltharaen keeps asking me what's on the Night Run. He asks it in that patient way he has, as though I've simply not got round to finding out.

And I keep telling him I don't know, and every time I say it I like myself a little less.

The wagons die on that road. That's the extent of our intelligence - that's what I have to send up to Astranaar, that wagons die there, which anyone could have told me from the wreckage.

Walk it. End to end, all of it.

And tell me what that road looks like to someone who isn't afraid of it, because I am no longer certain I can see it clearly.

The Night Run is the old road in the south-east corner of these woods, a long way from this post - down past the Moonwell and the lake, then east.

splintertree_lord_malgan.accept_text:
A tyrant who loses a ritual has two choices open to him. Try again, or die trying.

I have conducted enough interrogations to know which one Malgan will pick, and I have no intention of letting him get far enough into it to find out whether I'm right.

He holds the Throne by fear now rather than by strength. That is not the same thing and the satyrs under him know it even if he doesn't - you can hear it in how they move when he's in the open.

So I'll make the choice for him. He's at the Throne. Go and take it away from him.

Satyr's Throne is north of Splintertree. He has not left it, and he will not.

splintertree_voidwalkers.accept_text:
The remnants drift through the Demon Wastes, east of this wall, after dark.

They're not alive. They're not dead either, and I've had that argument with a priest and won it. They're not MADE for the world - that's the nearest I can get. Something summoned them here and then stopped paying attention, and they've been bumping along the inside of a place that doesn't want them ever since.

They're drifting closer to the wall every night. I've marked it.

Disperse them out there, before they get close enough to find out how thin this wall actually is. I know how thin it is. I'd prefer to keep that between us.
splintertree_voidwalkers.turn_in_text: The wall is quiet. I'll sleep tonight, which is more than I can say for the Wastes.

splintertree_pit_lord_emissary.accept_text:
It arrived with terms.

It has been standing in the Wastes for two days waiting for somebody of appropriate rank to come out and receive them, and in that time three of my scouts have gone close enough to hear the opening and come back changed in ways I am still assessing.

I do not read the terms of things that stand in fire. There is no version of this where we hear it out and come away with more than we started with - that is what an emissary IS, it is a creature whose entire function is to make the next thing sound reasonable.

Cut it off before it finishes a sentence. Preferably the first one.

It is waiting in the Demon Wastes, east of the post, for our answer. Take it one.
splintertree_pit_lord_emissary.turn_in_text: It was still talking when you reached it? Of course. They always are. I'll burn what's left of the terms.

splintertree_fel_imp_cache.accept_text:
Hinges. Buckles. A strip of my own mess-tent canvas, cut square.

The imps carry off the dumbest things out of this outpost and they stack them in the dirt out in the Wastes, and I have been going out there to look at the stacks, which I'd rather you didn't mention to the War Mage.

Here's the thing. It isn't a nest. I've seen nests and I've seen hoards and this is neither - it's ARRANGED, the same way every time, and a thief doesn't arrange.

I think it's a message and I think nobody told us how to read it.

Bring me scraps off them. Enough that I can lay it out the way they do and look at the whole of it at once.

The imps nest in the Demon Wastes, east of here. Whatever they are carrying, I want it back.

ashenvale_furbolg_ravagers.accept_text:
I want to tell you something about the furbolg before you go up that ridge, because it matters and because nobody your age was taught it.

We have shared this forest with them for a very long time. Not an alliance - we were never that formal about it. We simply both lived here and both knew where the other's ground was, and in all that time there was not a drop of blood between us worth recording.

Now the ravagers hold the ridge and they attack anything that crosses it. Anything. They have stopped distinguishing.

Something has changed them, and I have to get scouts in there to find out what. Thin the ravagers so that becomes possible - and while you're among them, LOOK at them. Properly. You'll see what I mean and I'd rather you saw it than took my word.

The ravagers hold the Ragged Highlands - north of Astranaar, past the lake and the Moonwell, in the north-east corner of the forest.

ashenvale_furbolg_shaman_totems.accept_text:
The ravagers aren't the cause. I've been certain of that since the second report and now I can prove it, which is a different thing.

They're being driven from behind. The shamans plant totems in the dens, and the madness is always worst where the totems are thickest - not where the fighting is, not at the ridge, in the DENS, at the carvings.

Bring me some of those totems out.

And carry them in cloth. I mean that as an order rather than advice: I will not have you holding one of those bare-handed across half a forest to spare yourself the trouble of a wrapping.

The shamans keep to the Ragged Highlands with the rest, north of Astranaar in the north-east corner of the forest.

ashenvale_ursal_the_mauler.accept_text:
Shalasyr sends word the totems are done. Good. Then whatever was feeding the Highland bears has stopped, and Ursal has nothing left driving him but his own temper - which, to be fair to him, has always been considerable.

He's the biggest of them and he's the one herding the others down toward the lake. That's been the shape of it all along: he moves, they move.

Go and finish it.

And do something for me. Before you do it, get a proper look at his eyes, and then come back and tell me honestly whether they were a bear's. I have asked three people that question and every one of them changed the subject.

He dens in the Ragged Highlands, east of this post.

splintertree_twilight_acolytes.accept_text:
Something under the Barrow is listening, and the acolytes are the ones doing the talking.

They go out at night and they whisper to the buried dead. Not chanting - whispering, the way you'd talk to somebody through a door, and you can stand on the mound and hear the shape of it without catching a word.

I don't know what's down there. I want to be extremely clear that I do not intend to find out by letting the conversation continue until it answers.

Silence the acolytes. Whatever is under that mound can go back to being a thing nobody has spoken to in a thousand years.

The Twilight Barrow is north-east of Splintertree, at the eastern edge of the forest.

splintertree_twilight_overseer.accept_text:
Every cult has somebody in it who is not a believer. Only a boss.

You can pick him out at a distance if you know what to look for: he is the one who doesn't look up during the important part. The acolytes were whispering FOR somebody, and it was him.

Kill him and the rest scatter - or they come for you, which is a better fight than the one we'll be having if whatever is under that Barrow learns to speak for itself.

I would rather fight a hundred frightened cultists than one patient thing underground with a voice.

You will find him where you found the acolytes - the Twilight Barrow, north-east of Splintertree.

splintertree_timber_quota.accept_text:
Orgrimmar wants timber. I want my loggers alive. For most of my career those have been the same objective and lately they have not been.

The grizzlies have decided the stand north-west of here, up at the Warsong Lumber Camp, is theirs. They come in at the crews, in daylight, which bears do not do unless something is very wrong with the arrangement they'd normally keep with us.

Deal with the biggest of them.

And before you suggest it - yes, I could send word to the Warchief and ask for the quota to be adjusted on account of bears. I'm told he's very reasonable about this sort of thing.

That is precisely why I am asking you instead.
splintertree_timber_quota.turn_in_text: Done, and the quota's back on track. You're hired. Not formally. I don't do paperwork, but I'll remember your name.

ashenvale_nightsaber_thinning.turn_in_text: Good. I'll tell the next wagon driver. He will pretend not to cry, and then he'll buy you a drink.

splintertree_burning_blade_scouts.turn_in_text: That many. They guard more than I thought. I'll mark it on the map and show Vashj. You have the hands for this. I hope you have the stomach, too.

splintertree_charred_wolves.turn_in_text: All of them, and not a wolf among them behaved like a wolf. I owe you a drink and an apology to the dead ones. Nothing in the world should look at fire and stay.

ashenvale_commander_spiders.turn_in_text: The road is clear. I will say this plainly: I did not expect to thank a Horde blade today. I find that I do.

zoram_crab_traps.turn_in_text: That will fill it. I can already smell the pot. You've done an old man a kindness, and kindness is rare on this coast.

zoram_naga_coastguard.turn_in_text: That many. Hm. I'll build the fourth boat a little faster. You'll forgive me if I name it after you, I name them all after people who've been useful.

lumber_felling_season.turn_in_text: That's the stand clear. I owe you a few logs' worth of thanks. Take your pick of the leftover axes. They're not good, but they're mine.

lumber_silk_slings.turn_in_text: Clean, every one. Look at that, it doesn't even stretch. I'll make you a sling of your own. For a bear. Or a friend you hate.

raynewood_cats.turn_in_text: The retreat is quiet. I will say a thing I haven't said to a stranger in years: thank you.

raynewood_vigil_lights.turn_in_text: That will see us through the new moon. Walk carefully out there. I'd rather not add you to the vigil.
